_what: Every choice of the current run. FEATURES.md says what each means.

years._what: puf: the PUF's tax year (its records, cut points and dollar maps); target: the year of the file the tilt makes and of its targets (SOI, SCF wave, CEX year, non-filer pool).

tax_units._what: The shared tax-unit rules (tax_units.py), run on every survey's member list (roster_cps.py, roster_scf.py, roster_cex.py). TAX_UNITS.md, section 4.
tax_units._reassign: CBO's reassignment pass (4c): true is CBO's default; false applies the first assignment only. The SCF and CEX (roster_scf.py, roster_cex.py) read it; the CPS's tax_units.py takes --strict.
tax_units._npeu_split: The SCF's adults outside the primary economic unit: how the group's income is divided among them. equal: equally; moore: wages among those under 70 and Social Security and pensions among those 62 and over (Moore's rule). The group's balance sheet is divided equally either way.

training._precision: fp32 standard 32-bit; tf32 or bf16 cheaper formats for the training steps only (train.py). Tested 22 October (explore/2026-10-22/perf/precision/PRECISION.md): bf16 37% faster a pass, results within the difference between two seeds.
training._shares_shown_with_their_base: Step 2 (train.py, model.gate_shares): on CPS rows the spouse's share of the couple's wages (of its self-employment income) is left out of a record whenever married or the share's base is hidden, so its presence never tells the network what those hidden slots hold; needed to draw non-filers' married flag and amounts under the CPS label. false: as before step 2.

translation._what: Translation (translate.py): one row per survey and variable it shares with the PUF; a variable not here is not shared. Every comparison is against the tax data for the survey's year: PUF filers other than dependent filers, weights scaled by SOI Table 1.6 (filing status x age), dollars grown per return with the item, and the CPS units of that year (or the nearest CPS year) weighted by their chance of not filing. items: the survey's columns, summed; an empty list is zero (an item the survey does not ask). Definition fixes: first_year (asked from this tax year; earlier years zero), part (positive: the positive part; loss: the size of the loss, stored positive), loss_cap. loss_cap: a definition fix, losses read as no more than this. Function 1, dollar_line (PUF-year dollars, grown to the survey's year per return): amounts within the line of zero keep their dollars; amounts beyond it get the tax data's amount at the same count from the top (losses: from the bottom); null is dollars throughout, 0 is rank throughout. Function 2, fill_in (fillin.py): the two-slot fill-in on function 1's bands, with the size ranges where reporting rates are read; it conditions on the variables with type_for_fill_in (and the survey year), which cannot have it themselves. Default: dollars, no fill-in; a departure gives its reason. report_lines: the dollar lines (survey-year dollars) of the report's size ranges.

translation._cps_zero_in_tax_data: PUF amounts the CPS has no row for (absent on CPS rows) that the CPS units in the tax data carry as zero. interest (John, 23 October): the CPS has no interest item lined up with the PUF's taxable interest.

cex._what: The CEX interview survey as a third source (build_cex.R, build_table.py): survey years 2015, 2017, 2019, 2021, 2023 and 2024, one row per tax unit and quarterly interview; every tax unit trains, a shared household's spending divided by head count (build_cex.R); dependent filers are folded into the unit that claims them, and the file's own dependent filers get no consumption. The 8 consumption categories are CEX-only slots, drawn last at generation under the CEX label and generation_year; dollars from that year's records. Shared with the PUF: married, dependents, age range, wages, gross Social Security (ss_gross) and self-employment income. The tilt's consumption targets come from the target year's CEX, all tax units.

cps._what: The CPS ASEC as a fourth source (build_cps.R): TAX years (the ASEC of March of the next year), every tax unit of the household population by CBO's rules (tax_units.py, the shared tax-unit module) as step 1 built them, filers and non-filers; dependent filers folded into the unit that claims them. p_file (the table's filer_p) is the return's calibrated filing chance from step 1 (its separate returns, filing status and statutory requirement come from step 1 too); training draws the filing flag from it in every pass. filer is one draw from it, one uniform per unit seeded by filer_seed plus the year, kept for the table's checks and reports. generation_year: the CPS label's year at generation. The CPS-only slots (build_table.py, CPS_AMOUNTS and CPS_CATEGORIES): exact ages and sex of the primary filer and spouse, dependents' ages, the spouse's share of the couple's wages and of its self-employment income, weeks and usual hours worked, childcare; drawn last at generation under the CPS label and generation_year. dollar_amounts: the CPS-only amounts in dollars, grown from the generation year to the target year by SOI's wages per return.
cps._mfs_split: Married filing separately as a post-filing step (tax_units.mfs_split): off by default. When on, a share of joint filer couples chosen by a draw keyed by unit id (salt filer_seed) become two separate returns, to SOI's Table 1.6 count; dependents by mfs_dep_rule.
cps._step1_dir: Step 1's folder (PLAN_v2.md step 1), required: the roster from <step1_dir>/units/roster_<year>_<cbo_variant>_nogq.csv.gz and step 1's returns from <step1_dir>/<step1_out>/units_<year>.csv.gz.
cps._step1_out: The folder inside step1_dir that holds step 1's returns (units_<year>.csv.gz), required: out_rule_v4, step 1's filing rule v4.

ages._what: The primary filer's age range (ages.py). Step 0 for PUF records with no range: a logit prior from the return, calibrated to SOI Table 1.6 less the known-range weight in each filing status x AGI cell where at least min_missing_share of the weight has no range. Survey couples: the man is the primary, except the woman with a chance by the man's range that reproduces the PUF's female-primary share by range; same-sex couples, the older partner.

generation._what: A stack of four strata of 100,000 PUF records each. Each oversamples the top 1% of one variable (the bands covering the top 1% of its positive weight drawn ten times as often) and carries importance weights that undo it. PUF variables are drawn in a random order per record; the computed totals are then computed from their parts; the balance sheet is drawn last, under the SCF label, with the PUF-only variables left out. The fourth stratum oversamples business equity, the most concentrated item of the balance sheet (net worth itself is computed, not drawn). Each stratum's seed fixes its draws.
generation._nonfiler_records: Step 2: the non-filer batch, drawn from the CPS label at the target year with the filing flag 0, no oversampling, every weight 1. null: its number of records is the filer strata's total (records_per_file x 4) times the CPS's expected non-filers in the target year (sum of weight x (1 - filer_p)) over SOI's returns that year; a number fixes it. nonfiler_seed fixes its draws.

consistency._what: Consistency rules at generation: when any item in when_any_nonzero is nonzero on the record, at least one holding in then_at_least_one_nonzero must be nonzero (generate.py says how). offset_generations: how many times generation runs; after each run but the last, each ruled holding's odds of being nonzero are scaled by one factor so that, with the rules, its expected holders equal the model's own. 1 means no offset.

rules.name: a partnership or S corporation item

tilt._what: Reweighting to 2019: the 136 IRS targets and the non-filer count exact; the people in non-filer units exact (heads and spouses in 7 age bands by their own exact age, and children under 17 among the head, spouse and first three dependents), the numbers step 1's calibration hit, read from nonfiler_targets_dir (<year>_nonfilers_vs_targets.csv), nonfiler_fallback_tolerance if the exact tilt does not converge even with the business and age fallbacks; filers' returns by the primary filer's age range, 26-34 to 65+, from SOI Table 1.6, in joint and in non-joint returns (age_level "filing_status"; "all" for the five totals; "none" for no age targets), exact (age_fallback_tolerance if the exact tilt does not converge even with the business fallback), dependent filers 26 and over spread over those ranges by Table 1.6's shares, under 26 left to the total and joint counts; the SOI business targets exact (2% if the exact tilt does not converge), estates and trusts left out until the targeting overhaul; the eight SCF 2019 wealth targets with a 2% tolerance, counts as shares of the file's units other than dependent filers. Filers' starting weights pre-scaled to the 2019 joint and non-joint return counts. Consumption: the 8 categories' CEX 2019 averages per tax unit, overall and in 12 cells of the primary filer's adult age range by married (a joint unit; separate returns are not married, on both sides), dependent filers left out on both sides (104 targets), within consumption_band of each average (free inside the band).
